title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
summary: The Great Wave off Kanagawa  is a woodblock print by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Hokusai (1760–1849), created in late 1831 during the Edo period of Japanese history. The print depicts three boats moving through a storm-tossed sea, with a large, cresting wave forming a spiral in the centre over the boats and Mount Fuji in the background.

sections.name: the great wave
sections.description: The massive, cresting wave dominates the left side of the composition, its dark blue water and white foam claws threatening the boats below.

sections.name: the great wave's crest
sections.description: The massive, claw-like crest of the wave, frozen at its peak, symbolizes the overwhelming power of nature.

sections.name: Mount Fuji
sections.description: The snow-capped peak of Mount Fuji appears small in the distance, framed by the curve of the wave, representing permanence amidst the chaos.

sections.name: a boat and its rowers
sections.description: A third boat in the foreground is surrounded by churning blue water, emphasizing the scale of the sea's turbulence.

museum_facts: Hokusai’s composition uses perspective to make Mount Fuji look like a small triangle nestled inside the hollow of the cresting wave.
The print is part of his Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series and dates to about 1830–32.
It is a Japanese woodblock print made with ink and color on paper, using a palette that includes indigo and imported Prussian blue.
The Met notes that the composition is said to have inspired Debussy’s La Mer and Rilke’s Der Berg.

guide_notes.the great wave: The big curve climbing from the bottom left to the top right is the back of the wave, and the straight line running back down inside it is its front face, so the wave towers over the whole board; the separate balls along the top are its spray. Hokusai made it as a woodblock print around 1831, and thousands of copies were printed from the carved blocks.
guide_notes.the great wave's crest: The arc that climbs up the left side and curls over to the right is the crest of the wave, with open space inside the curl. When the Metropolitan Museum examined this print, it found the deep blue inside the curl was printed twice, layer on layer.
guide_notes.Mount Fuji: Mount Fuji is the mountain outline, a small peak at the top with two slopes spreading down to a wide base along the bottom row; the broken line across the sixth row is where its snowcap ends. It looks tiny next to the wave, yet it is the subject of the whole series, Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
guide_notes.a boat and its rowers: The long rounded outline at the bottom is the boat's hull, the diagonal line rising to the top left is its pointed bow, and the row of separate balls on top are the rowers, crouched low. These were fast barges that rushed fresh fish to market, each with eight rowers and two more crew at the bow.
